questions.question: Why do AI startups often fail from cost issues rather than model quality?
options: Models are always good enough that startups can skip evaluation and cost tracking once the demo looks convincing — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
Cost optimization is easy because provider prompt caching alone cuts most bills by 90% with zero code changes
API providers offer unlimited free tiers for production traffic once a startup passes a few thousand daily users
Per-call costs compound rapidly: 10K users making 10 calls/day costs $250/day in tokens before charging a single dollar
questions.explanation: LLM API costs scale linearly with usage. A feature that costs fractions of a cent per call seems cheap until it's called hundreds of thousands of times a day. Without cost optimization, many AI products are unprofitable at scale.

questions.question: What is semantic caching for LLM applications?
options: Caching the model's weights in memory between requests so the same GPU doesn't reload them for every call
Storing responses for previous queries and serving cached responses when a new query is semantically similar (not just exactly matching)
Caching only the query embeddings themselves, without ever storing or reusing the LLM's generated response
Pre-generating every possible response ahead of time and serving from that fixed table instead of calling the API, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
questions.explanation: Exact-match caching only helps with identical queries. Semantic caching embeds queries and serves cached responses when cosine similarity exceeds a threshold. 'What's the weather in NYC?' matches 'NYC weather today?'.

questions.question: What is model routing as a cost optimization strategy?
options: Load balancing identical requests across multiple servers running the same model to reduce latency under traffic
Sending simple queries to cheap/fast models and complex queries to expensive/powerful models based on query classification
Routing every request between different API providers at random purely to average out each vendor's per-token pricing, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
Caching responses from multiple models and returning whichever cached answer arrives first regardless of quality
questions.explanation: Not every query needs the most expensive model. A classifier routes simple questions (FAQ, greetings) to a cheap model and complex questions (reasoning, analysis) to an expensive model. This can cut costs 40-70%.

questions.question: What is prompt compression and how does it reduce costs?
options: Making prompts shorter by deleting words at random until the token count falls under a fixed per-request budget, without regard to meaning

Compressing the prompt text with a binary algorithm like gzip before sending it as the request payload, the same way you would compress a file, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path
Using shorter variable and function names in the application code that builds the prompt, which has no effect on the billed input tokens
Removing redundant tokens, summarizing long contexts, and eliminating boilerplate to reduce input token count while preserving essential information
questions.explanation: Input tokens dominate cost in RAG applications (large retrieved contexts). Prompt compression removes filler words, summarizes verbose passages, and trims low-relevance chunks to reduce token count without losing key information.

questions.question: What is prefix caching and which provider feature enables it?
options: Caching only the first generated word of each response so the model can start streaming the rest of the answer faster next time — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
Caching DNS lookups for the provider's API endpoint so every request skips domain name resolution before it even starts
Browser-side caching of API responses so a user's second identical request never reaches the provider's servers at all
Reusing KV-cache computation for shared prompt prefixes (system prompt + tool definitions), reducing latency and cost for repeated patterns
questions.explanation: If your system prompt + tool definitions are 5000 tokens and identical across requests, prefix caching computes the KV-cache once and reuses it. Anthropic's prompt caching and OpenAI's cached tokens both support this.

questions.question: What is the best completion criterion for Caching, Rate Limiting & Cost Optimization?
options: Calculate per-request costs across providers and implement token-aware rate limiting and budget alerts
Skip validation and trust the first plausible-looking output
Choose a production framework before defining the core mechanism, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
Treat one successful example as proof that every edge case works
questions.explanation: “Calculate per-request costs across providers and implement token-aware rate limiting and budget alerts” is one of this lesson’s stated outcomes; the other choices bypass its required reasoning or validation.
